subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Pikes Peak: Race to the Clouds
description: A 60-second lesson on Pikes Peak: Race to the Clouds.

hook.text: Pikes Peak is a 12.4-mile hill climb up a Colorado mountain to an altitude of 14,115 feet.

buildup.text: At the summit, the air has 40 percent less oxygen—engines lose power and brakes overheat.

discovery.text: One side of the road drops off a cliff with no guardrail—one mistake means a thousand-foot fall.

twist.text: In 2018, an electric VW ID.R obliterated the record, proving EVs thrive where thin air chokes engines.

climax.text: Pikes Peak remains the ultimate test of machine and courage at the edge of the atmosphere.

punchline.text: The race to the clouds is where electric cars finally shine.

quiz.question: Why do electric cars have an advantage at Pikes Peak?
options: They don't lose power in thin air like combustion engines

details.summary: The Pikes Peak International Hill Climb challenges drivers to race 12.42 miles up a Colorado mountain to 14,115 feet, where thin air robs engines of power but electric motors thrive without oxygen.
details.whyItMatters: Pikes Peak became a proving ground for electric vehicles when Volkswagen's ID.R demolished the overall record in 2018, demonstrating that EVs can outperform combustion cars in extreme conditions.
takeaways: The course climbs from 9,390 to 14,115 feet above sea level
Thin air at altitude reduces combustion engine power by 30 percent
Volkswagen's electric ID.R set the overall course record in 2018

faq.question: Why do electric cars have an advantage at Pikes Peak?
faq.answer: Electric motors do not need air to produce power. At 14,000 feet, combustion engines lose roughly 30 percent of their power due to thin air, while electric motors deliver full power regardless of altitude.

faq.question: Is the entire Pikes Peak course paved?
faq.answer: It has been fully paved since 2011. Before that, the upper sections were gravel, making the race even more dangerous. The smoother surface allows much higher speeds but also demands more precise driving.
